title: Temperature alarm
summary: Convert an analog reading to °C and raise an alarm.
goal: When the TMP36 on A0 reads above 40 °C, turn on the LED on pin 13 and print "ALARM". Below that, keep the LED off and stay quiet.
brief:
A **TMP36** temperature sensor outputs a voltage: 500 mV at 0 °C, plus 10 mV for every degree. It is wired to **A0**.

`analogRead(A0)` returns 0 to 1023 for 0 to 5 V, so:

```
volts = reading * 5.0 / 1023.0
tempC = (volts - 0.5) * 100.0
```

1. Read A0 a few times per second and convert the reading to °C.
2. Above 40 °C: LED on and print `ALARM`.
3. Otherwise: LED off, print nothing alarming.

The check starts the room at 25 °C and heats it to 50 °C at 2 s.
hints: analogRead gives a number from 0 to 1023, not a voltage. Convert it to volts first.
Use float, not int: (reading * 5.0 / 1023.0 - 0.5) * 100.0. Integer division throws the decimals away.
float tempC = (analogRead(SENSOR_PIN) * 5.0 / 1023.0 - 0.5) * 100.0; if (tempC > ALARM_C) { digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH); Serial.println("ALARM"); } else { digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW); } delay(200);
